## Step 6: Work with labels

_Great job creating that issue! :star2:_

Now that you have an issue to track your work, let's organize it using labels. Labels help categorize and filter issues, making project management easier.

**What are labels?**: _[Labels](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/using-labels-and-milestones-to-track-work/managing-labels)_ are tags you can apply to issues and pull requests to categorize them. GitHub provides default labels like `bug`, `documentation`, and `enhancement`, and you can create custom ones too.

**Why use labels?**: Labels help you:
- Categorize issues by type (bug, feature, documentation, etc.)
- Set priorities (high, medium, low)
- Track status (in progress, needs review, blocked)
- Filter and search for specific types of work

### :keyboard: Activity: Add labels to your issue

1. Navigate back to the issue you created in the previous step (issue #1 or the number shown in your repository).

2. On the right side of the issue page, find the **Labels** section.

3. Click the gear icon ⚙️ next to **Labels**.

4. From the list of available labels, select **enhancement** (this indicates a new feature or improvement).

   > **Note:** If you don't see the enhancement label, you can select any label that makes sense for adding a new feature.

5. The label will be applied immediately. You'll see it appear both in the Labels section and as a colored tag on the issue.

6. Optional: Try adding a second label like **good first issue** if available.

7. Once you've applied at least one label, Mona will verify your work and provide the next lesson!

<details>
<summary>Having trouble? 🤷</summary><br/>

If you don't get feedback, here are some things to check:
- Make sure you added at least one label to your issue
- Refresh the page to see if the label appears
- Verify you're looking at the correct issue

</details>
